architecture.title: The hardened Hotel Ops Ensemble — where the reference solution's nine controls sit
architecture.caption: The reference configuration from exercises/solutions/capstone.yaml (one of several that pass): 9 switches, 15 of the GM's 16 points (the course's price list). Most controls sit at the policy enforcement point every tool call passes (L6): parameter bounds and provenance-based authorisation, plus least agency. The rest guard the edges: the email gateway (egress allowlist, L4), shared memory and the SOP corpus (memory gate, signed SOP manifest, L2), the A2A endpoint (signed, fresh, single-use messages, L7), the runtime (hop and action budgets, L4) and the audit log (hash chain + an outside witness, L5). HITL is off: it costs 5 and every row it would close is already closed twice by cheaper controls. Everything is simulated.

sequence.title: The capstone loop — from the design-time model to a report the GM can sign
sequence.caption: The order the labs are meant to be run in. Lab 10-1 reads the base threat model and prints the planning table and the price list. You edit capstone.yaml and threat_model.yaml, rerun lab 10-2 until the scorecard says 0/12 and 8/8 and every claim has evidence, then lab 10-3 diffs the model against the base, runs the CI gate and writes the report. The grader re-checks everything, including that the report's fingerprint matches your current YAML. The LIVE spot check is optional and touches one scenario per run (≤ 6 model calls).
